notes.author: Sleep medicine physician
notes.text:
Polysomnography Report
Date: 08/25/2025
Patient: Salvatore Mosciski, 75-year-old male

Diagnostic in-laboratory polysomnography performed 08/25/2025. Total apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) 27.2 events/hour. Central and mixed apneas comprised 13% of all events. Sleep stages were appropriately distributed with some arousals noted. Oxygen saturation levels showed intermittent drops associated with respiratory events. The study indicates moderate sleep apnea with a significant central component. Further clinical evaluation and treatment planning are recommended.

Sleep Medicine Consultation Note
Date: 08/02/2026
Patient: Salvatore Mosciski, 76-year-old male

Reason for Consultation:
Evaluation and management of sleep-disordered breathing.

History:
Mr. Mosciski is a 76-year-old male with a history of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) diagnosed several years ago. He has been prescribed CPAP therapy but reports difficulty tolerating the device.

Physical Examination:
BMI 33.8 kg/m2.
No other significant findings noted on examination relevant to sleep disorder.

Assessment:
The patient demonstrates CPAP intolerance: download shows average use 1.3 hours per night on 32% of nights despite mask refitting; shared decision-making with the patient documented that CPAP is not tolerated.

Plan:
Discuss alternative treatment options including positional therapy, oral appliance therapy, and lifestyle modifications such as weight management.
Referral to dental sleep specialist for evaluation of oral appliance suitability.
Continue monitoring symptoms and consider repeat sleep study if clinically indicated.

Follow-up:
Patient to return in 3 months or sooner if symptoms worsen.

Summary:
Mr. Mosciski has documented CPAP intolerance despite efforts to optimize mask fit and adherence. Alternative therapies will be explored to manage his sleep apnea effectively.
